property_summary: Only calls from the contract owner can successfully call sendTo (non-owners cause it to revert).
Only transactions originating from the contract owner succeed in calling sendTo; calls from non-owners revert.
If caller equals this contract address then the call to c.sendTo must not revert; otherwise it must revert.
If caller equals this contract then the call to c.sendTo must not revert; otherwise it must revert.

Only the owner can cause ether to be transferred out of the contract via sendTo; the mutant removes that restriction allowing non-owners to drain funds, so the rule is: after any call to sendTo by a non-owner with value > 0, the contract balance remains unchanged (reference reverts / disallows) — the mutant allows balance decrease for some inputs.

For any caller who is not the owner, calling sendTo(...) must revert (so address(c).balance cannot be decreased by non-owners); the mutant removes the owner check and thus allows a non-owner to successfully transfer out contract balance for some fuzzed inputs.
Only the contract owner can successfully call sendTo to transfer ether from the contract (non-owners cannot).
Calls to c.sendTo(...) succeed (do not revert) iff the caller is the contract owner; in particular, when msg.sender equals the owner the call must not revert.
Calls to c.sendTo(...) revert exactly when msg.sender is not the owner (i.e., only the owner can call without revert).
If the call to c.sendTo(receiver, amount) did not revert then reverted == (msg.sender != msg.sender) (i.e., the test's existing assert holds).
If the external call to c.sendTo(receiver, amount) does not revert then the asserted relation reverted == (msg.sender != msg.sender) holds (i.e., the test's single assert must be preserved).
Only the owner can successfully call sendTo; the mutant inverts this and allows non-owners while blocking the owner, so there exist calls where owner succeeds on reference but fails on mutant.

For every caller and amount, calls to sendTo succeed iff the caller is the contract owner (reference allows owner to send funds; the mutant blocks owner and thus for some inputs the owner-call that should succeed will fail).

For every caller address and payable amount where the contract has sufficient balance, sendTo succeeds when invoked by the contract owner (reference allows owner to call), but the mutant inverts the require and will cause a call from the owner to fail for some inputs.

For any caller and amount, a call to sendTo(...) succeeds when invoked by the contract owner (so address(c).balance decreases by amount) — the mutant inverts the require and will make owner calls fail for some inputs.

For any caller who is the owner and any amount <= contract balance, calling sendTo transfers exactly that amount (so address(c).balance decreases by amount); the mutant that calls transfer twice can make address(c).balance decrease by 2*amount, violating this rule for some fuzzed amount.

For any caller who is the owner and any nonzero amount no greater than the contract balance, a single call to sendTo reduces address(c).balance by exactly that amount; the mutant that transfers twice can reduce the balance by twice the amount, violating this rule for some fuzzed amounts.

For any owner caller and any amount <= contract balance, a single call to sendTo either succeeds and reduces address(c).balance by exactly amount (reference) — the mutant that transfers twice can reduce balance by 2*amount for some fuzzed amount, violating this rule.

For any recipient address and any amount where the caller is the contract owner and the contract holds at least that amount, a single call to sendTo will not transfer more than the contract balance (i.e., address(c).balance after the call is >= 0 and decreased by at most the sent amount); the mutant that transfers twice can make the contract balance decrease by twice the amount, violating that the balance never decreases by more than the supplied amount.

For any caller who is the contract owner and any amount x (0 <= x <= address(c).balance), a single call to sendTo(receiver, x) decreases address(c).balance by exactly x; the mutant that transfers twice can decrease address(c).balance by 2*x for some fuzzed inputs, breaking this equality.

For any caller who is the owner and any amount, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) transfers ether out of the contract balance to the specified receiver so that address(c).balance decreases by that amount; the mutant that always transfers to owner breaks this when receiver != owner because the contract balance does not decrease by amount (it instead stays the same or decreases differently).

For any caller who is the contract owner and any payable amount, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) will reduce address(c).balance by exactly amount (the reference transfers to the specified receiver); the mutant that always transfers to owner violates this when receiver != owner because the contract balance does not decrease by amount to the receiver.

For any caller who is the owner and for any nonzero amount up to the contract balance, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) will change the recipient's balance when receiver != owner (i.e., the specified receiver's balance increases by amount); the mutant that redirects transfers to owner breaks this because the specified receiver's balance does not increase for some inputs.

For any caller that is the contract owner and any receiver address, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) will not increase the owner's balance by exactly amount (i.e. the specified receiver receives the amount, so owner's balance does not increase by amount); the mutant that redirects the transfer to owner breaks this because the owner's balance increases by amount when receiver != owner.

For any caller equal to the contract owner and any receiver address that is a contract whose fallback reverts, calling sendTo(receiver, amount) on the correct contract will revert (because transfer to a reverting contract fails), but the mutant that redirects the transfer to owner (an EOA owner) will succeed for some fuzzed inputs — so the universal property: if receiver is a reverting contract and caller==owner then sendTo must revert; the mutant breaks this by transferring to owner instead of receiver and not reverting.
